gaps: CONCURRENT REDDIT MULTI-ACCOUNT IS IMPOSSIBLE WITH THE KEPT TRANSPORT. The plan's headline architecture (`adapters constructed per (instance, account) pair, never global singletons, so Reddit+Lemmy AND multiple Reddit accounts coexist simultaneously`) is only true for Lemmy. Verified in utils/RedditCookies.ts and utils/safeFetch.ts: Reddit auth rides a process-GLOBAL native cookie jar keyed by host (`CookieManager.get('https://www.reddit.com')` returns the one-and-only `reddit_session`), and safeFetch (XHR) sends whatever cookie is currently in that jar implicitly. Hydra supports multi-account only by SWAPPING cookies on switch (restoreSessionCookies), which is serial. De-globalizing only `UserAuth.modhash` (the one structural change the plan emphasizes) does NOT fix this; two Reddit adapters with different accounts issuing concurrent authenticated requests will collide on the shared `www.reddit.com` cookie. The plan never addresses making cookies per-request/per-instance, which would require rewriting the transport to pass Cookie headers explicitly (and abandoning the native cookie jar the WebView login depends on).

LEMMY uploadImage TAKES A BROWSER `File`. Verified in services/lemmy.ts: `_uploadImage(..., image: File, ...)` and `reduceFileSize` (web canvas via helpers/imageCompress). The plan acknowledges this as 'highest-risk' but defers it to a Phase 0 .d.ts read and a generic 'port to expo-image-manipulator.' The gap: the unified SourceAdapter.uploadImage signature already commits to `JanusFile = {uri, mimeType, name}`, but whether threadiverse's own uploadImage accepts anything other than a browser File/Blob is UNKNOWN and unverifiable (package not installed). If threadiverse internally constructs FormData with a File, expo file objects will not work and the adapter must bypass threadiverse for upload entirely — which the plan's 'adopt threadiverse directly' posture forbids.

DEEP-THREAD COMMENT PAGING IS UNMODELED. Verified Voyager calls `client.getComments({ max_depth, page_cursor, parent_id })` — Lemmy returns a bounded-depth subtree and uses BOTH a page_cursor AND parent_id continue-thread fetches AND child_count-derived 'missing' counts. The unified `getComments(postId, {parentId?, maxDepth?} & PageRequest)` plus a single `LoadMoreRef = {depth, childIds: string[], nativeCursor?}` conflates three different continuation mechanisms (Reddit `more.childIds` string list; Lemmy `parent_id` subtree fetch; Lemmy `child_count - present` missing count). `childIds: string[]` has no meaning for Lemmy, and `nativeCursor` has no meaning for Reddit's `more` nodes. The 'one CommentTree builder fed flat comments from both' is underspecified for how load-more re-enters the tree.

THE 'THIN MECHANICAL MAPPER' IS NOT THIN. api/Posts.ts is 440 lines and api/PostDetail.ts is 367 lines of Reddit-specific extraction producing Hydra's idiosyncratic media shape `images: (string | ImageSource[])[]` and `videos: {source, videoDownloadURL}[]`. The plan maps Hydra Post -> unified Post via a 'thin, mechanical layer,' but the UI components key off those exact quirky shapes, so the unified MediaItem[] must round-trip back into `(string|ImageSource[])[]` for the kept components — meaning you maintain BOTH the unified model AND Hydra's media shape, not a clean replacement. The plan's MediaItem entity does not capture the nested-array gallery ordering semantics.

RATE-LIMIT/BACKOFF HARDENING IS DEFERRED TO PHASE 4 BUT IS A PHASE-1 CORRECTNESS ISSUE. The findings are emphatic: Hydra has NO 429/Retry-After/backoff/concurrency handling anywhere, and Janus centralizes traffic. The plan defers backoff to Phase 4 'hardening,' but the source-agnostic feed engine and depaginate recursion are built in Phases 1-2; retrofitting concurrency limits and backoff into an already-shipped feed engine is far harder than designing the PageRequest/transport contract for it up front. The SourceAdapter interface has no place to express rate-limit state or Retry-After.

NO STRATEGY FOR REDDIT JSON SCHEMA DRIFT AT THE ADAPTER BOUNDARY. Findings note heavy `any` use in formatters means schema drift fails at runtime. The plan's adapter boundary is typed (unified domain model) but does nothing to validate Reddit's untyped JSON before mapping; a Reddit shape change still fails silently inside the mapper. No runtime validation / schema-guard layer is proposed.

SNUDOWN AND old.reddit.com DEPENDENCIES ARE FLAGGED 'OUT' BUT THE FEATURES THAT NEED THEM (compose preview, submit, gated/quarantine accept, prefs) are in scope. Submit is in SubmitPostInput on the interface; the plan defers snudown and the old.reddit submit path to 'decide later,' leaving the write path with an undefined markdown-preview and submit transport.
contradictions: 'helpers/lemmy.ts ... pure TS, zero web deps ... lift verbatim/wholesale' is FALSE as verified. helpers/lemmy.ts imports `quote` from helpers/markdown.ts (a full unified + rehype-parse + rehype-remark + remark-stringify pipeline) and `parseUrl` from helpers/url.ts, which references `document.location.href` — a DOM global absent in React Native/Hermes. So the file the plan says to copy verbatim has a transitive DOM dependency and a heavy markdown pipeline. The pure-tree functions (buildCommentsTree/getCommentParentId/getDepthFromCommentPath) ARE pure, but you cannot lift the file wholesale; you must surgically extract and break the markdown/url imports.

'api/* modules ... no React imports' / 'zero React imports' is overstated. Verified: api/RedditApi.ts and api/Posts.ts both `import { Alert } from 'react-native'` and call Alert.alert; api/PostDetail.ts imports modifyStat from db/functions/Stats and calls it. The plan's own redditAdapterPlan correctly lists these as needs-porting, but the architectureMap and recommendation repeatedly assert the api layer is 'already remarkably decoupled (pure async functions returning app-defined types, no React imports)' — which contradicts the react-native and db imports the plan elsewhere admits exist. The decoupling is real-ish but not 'no React imports.'

The plan flags Hydra AGPL-3.0 as the licensing risk but treats Voyager as merely a source of 'pure helpers to lift verbatim.' Verified: VOYAGER IS ALSO AGPL-3.0. Lifting Voyager helpers verbatim imposes the same copyleft as Hydra. The plan's licensing item names only Hydra, understating the exposure: the app is built from TWO AGPL codebases, so the AGPL question is not 'resolve before shipping closed-source' — it is effectively settled (the derived app is AGPL) unless code is rewritten clean-room.

The recommendation says 'Standardize state on Hydra's context+hooks pattern (not Voyager's Redux)' and 'Keep the optimistic-update-with-rollback business logic.' But Voyager's optimistic vote/save/rollback logic is implemented AS Redux thunks reading clientSelector(getState()) with parallel override dictionaries (postVotesById etc.) — the findings explicitly say 'optimistic updates assume synchronous getState() reads of override maps.' Porting that business logic OUT of Redux into Hydra's context+hooks is a rewrite, not a lift; the plan calls it 'port architecturally' in one place and 'keep the business logic' in another, eliding that the rollback mechanism is coupled to the very Redux store the plan discards.

Capabilities object lists supportsAwards (reddit true, lemmy no) and supportsPolls (reddit true), but the findings state Hydra OMITS awards entirely and STUBS poll voting (PollViewer alert('voted')). So declaring reddit supportsAwards=true / supportsPolls=true advertises capabilities the kept Reddit layer does not actually implement — the UI would show controls that do nothing.
underestimatedRisks: THE ENTIRE LEMMY HALF RESTS ON AN UNINSPECTED PRE-1.0 SINGLE-MAINTAINER PACKAGE. Confirmed threadiverse is NOT in node_modules and was never read; every threadiverse method signature, PageCursor shape, NotificationView consolidation, and uploadImage File/Blob behavior in the plan is INFERRED from Voyager call sites. The plan correctly makes this Phase 0, but the architectural commitment ('LemmyAdapter does NOT code against raw lemmy-js-client; it reuses threadiverse') is locked in BEFORE the spike result is known. If the Phase 0 read fails (DOM internals, browser-only upload, Hermes-incompatible), the plan says 'fall back to lemmy-js-client' — but that fallback discards the v0/v1/PieFed unification, sort-conversion tables, and NotificationView mapping the plan depends on, i.e. it is a different architecture, not a swap. Risk: committing the SourceAdapter contract and domain model to threadiverse's shapes (PageCursor-as-PageToken, NotificationView-as-Notification superset) before confirming threadiverse is RN-viable.

THE URL-AS-ROUTE REFACTOR IS UNDERESTIMATED AS A PHASE-1/2 ITEM. RedditURL throws 'Not a reddit URL' and conflates content-URL normalization, PageType classification, AND internal hydra:// app routing (settings sub-routing parses hydra://settings/... relative paths). pushURL(string) is called by dozens of components and pages re-parse `new RedditURL(route.params.url)` internally. The plan acknowledges 'highest blast radius' but schedules the typed-Route migration in Phase 2 AFTER the RedditAdapter is built against the new id/route model in Phase 1 — meaning Phase 1 must already produce permalinkRoute descriptors while the route system is still URL-strings, creating a half-migrated state across the entire component tree.

PROVIDER ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING, UNDOCUMENTED, AND COUPLED TO PRO-GATING. Verified ThemeContext directly imports SubscriptionsContext and reads {isPro, purchasesInitialized}; Theme depends on Subscriptions, Navigation depends on Account+Theme. The plan recommends 'dropping pro-gating for v1 to simplify provider ordering' but also inserts a NEW source-selection/AccountManager provider that must hydrate async (Lemmy JWT) BEFORE adapters are constructed. Reordering this stack to add async-hydrate-before-adapter while removing the Subscriptions->Theme edge is a high-risk surgery on an undocumented initialization sequence; a wrong order yields blank-theme or no-adapter cold starts.

ACCOUNT-SWITCH STATE-RESET FAN-OUT IS A PRIVACY BUG WAITING TO HAPPEN. Findings: Voyager's resetAccountSpecificStoreData() fans out to ~every content slice; 'missing a slice on port leaves stale cross-account data (privacy/correctness risk).' Janus is abandoning Redux for Hydra's context+hooks, so it must RE-DERIVE this fan-out across a different (and not-yet-designed) state layer, AND now also reset across SOURCES (Reddit<->Lemmy) and instances, not just accounts. The plan mentions this only in Phase 4 QA. Cross-source data bleed is harder than Voyager's because Hydra's seen_posts/favorites are currently global.

ToS / BAN RISK AT CENTRALIZED SCALE IS TREATED AS A LATE HARDENING ITEM, NOT A FOUNDATION RISK. Hydra's no-API-key web-session scraping works at one-user-per-device scale precisely BECAUSE traffic is distributed across users' own IPs/sessions. The plan inherits this verbatim as the product foundation. If Janus ever adds any server-side component (the plan keeps open the server inbox-polling option that ships raw reddit_session off-device), Reddit-side bot detection and IP bans become a single-point product-killing risk. The randomized UA is explicitly called 'weak evasion.' This is a product-viability risk, not a Phase 4 backlog item.

SHIPPING reddit_session OFF-DEVICE: the plan 'defaults to on-device polling only' but leaves server polling as an option. A full Reddit account session leaving the device is a severe privacy exposure; offering it as a toggle still requires building the secured server path, and the decision interacts with App Store review and Reddit ToS.
domainModelHoles: COMMENT `path` / `parentId` TYPE MISMATCH. Verified: Voyager getCommentParentId returns `Number(...)` from a dotted-numeric `path` string ('0.123.456'); Lemmy ids are numeric DB ids. Hydra Comment.path is `number[]` (synthesized), but Hydra comment identity is the `t1_xxx` fullname STRING and Reddit loadMore.childIds are STRING fullnames. The unified Comment has `id: JanusId` (string) and `parentId?: JanusId` (string), which is fine at the boundary, but the plan's claim that one CommentTree builder consumes 'flat comments with parentId/depth from both' hides that Reddit parent linkage comes from a number[] path Hydra fabricated while Lemmy's comes from server-authoritative dotted numeric paths with child_count semantics. The 'missing replies' concept is count-based on Lemmy (child_count minus present) and child-id-list-based on Reddit; these are not the same data and LoadMoreRef cannot represent both cleanly.

scoreHidden IS REDDIT-ONLY. Verified Hydra Comment has scoreHidden (from score_hidden); the Voyager lemmy helper has no score_hidden / hide_score. The unified Post and Comment list scoreHidden: boolean as if symmetric; for Lemmy it is always false (Lemmy has no hide-score), so a 'unified' field is actually a Reddit-only field defaulted — fine, but the model presents it as shared, and the same pattern (isStickied vs featured_local/featured_community, distinguished, interactionStatus locked/archived vs Lemmy locked-only) hides several Reddit-only-or-asymmetric fields behind a falsely-symmetric schema.

Community.handle and subscription='pending' encode real divergence the model half-acknowledges but the ID codec fights. JanusId = source:instance:kind:nativeId, but for Lemmy the SAME community exists under many instance-qualified handles via federation; keying JanusId on the LOCAL instance you fetched from means the same logical community gets DIFFERENT JanusIds depending on which instance served it. The plan says 'always derive identity/dedup from ap_id+local' in the adapter, but JanusId itself is built from `instance:nativeId`, not ap_id — so the canonical id and the dedup key diverge, exactly the federation collision the findings warn about. resolveRemoteUrl returns a JanusId, but two JanusIds can denote one ap_id object.

Notification model unifies on Lemmy-1.0 NotificationView as 'a superset,' but 0.19 (the most-deployed) has DISCRETE getReplies/getPersonMentions/getUnreadCount with CommentReplyView/PersonMentionView shapes, and Reddit has t1 CommentReply + t4 Message with modmail/threading semantics. Mapping Reddit modmail conversations (getConversationMessages, threaded) onto a flat NotificationView discriminated union is lossy; Reddit private-message THREADS have no clean NotificationView analog, and the plan's sendMessage/getInbox interface flattens conversation threading.

Top-sort-as-(sort x duration) product (Lemmy) vs Reddit bundling top+timeWindow is captured via topRequiresTimeWindow + needsTimeWindow, which is good — but the per-mode Lemmy sort tables (lemmyv0 'TopAll' string vs lemmyv1 {sort:'top', time_range_seconds} vs piefed) are a mode-discriminated UNION, not a flat SortOption{id,label,needsTimeWindow}. The unified SortOption cannot express the v0-vs-v1-vs-piefed shape divergence the findings call 'the main cross-version translation surface'; convertSortToLemmyParams must live entirely inside the adapter and the capability's SortOption.id becomes an opaque token, undermining the idea that the shell reads capability sorts directly.

Crossposts: Reddit crossPost is a nested first-class Post (supportsCrossposts='firstClass'); Lemmy crossposts are URL-GROUPED detection ('urlGrouped'), not an object. MediaItem kind:'crosspost' models the Reddit nested-post case but there is no representation for Lemmy's 'these N posts share a URL' grouping, which is a feed-level concern, not a per-post media item — the model has no home for it.
verdict: Not yet sound enough to start building Phase 1 as written. The layering instinct (one shell, two adapters behind one SourceAdapter, namespaced JanusIds, capability-driven UI) is correct and worth pursuing, and the findings genuinely support keeping Hydra's components and wrapping its decoupled-ish api layer. But three load-bearing claims are wishful or wrong against the actual code: (1) 'per-(instance,account) adapters coexist simultaneously' is false for Reddit because the kept transport rides a single global native cookie jar — de-globalizing only modhash does not fix concurrent multi-account; (2) 'lift Voyager helpers/lemmy.ts verbatim, pure/zero web deps' is false — it transitively pulls in a DOM global (document.location.href via helpers/url) and a heavy unified/rehype markdown pipeline; (3) the whole Lemmy half is committed to threadiverse whose RN-viability is literally uninspectable in this repo. THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FIX BEFORE PHASE 1: do the Phase 0 threadiverse spike (install, read .d.ts, run under Hermes, prove uploadImage accepts an RN file) AND, equally, prototype the Reddit transport's auth model to prove whether multiple accounts can be active concurrently — i.e. decide now whether Janus passes Cookie headers explicitly per-request (rewriting safeFetch and breaking the WebView-shared-cookie-jar login) or accepts that Reddit is single-active-account-at-a-time. That auth-concurrency decision reshapes AccountManager, the SourceAdapter contract, and the entire 'unify two account models' premise, and it must be settled before any adapter code is written. Secondary but mandatory: treat AGPL as settled (both upstreams are AGPL-3.0) and design rate-limit/backoff into the transport and the SourceAdapter contract up front rather than as Phase 4 hardening.
